rationale:
Evidence: iteration 0 (score 53.0) is the best design so far. Iteration 1 (score 50.6) changed ki, kp, kd and base_speed together, and its s-bend result (progress 0.1475, identical to iteration 0) did not move. The round-1 critique is right that my draft changed five or more factors at once (sensor size, sensor offset, kp, kd, ki, base_speed, mass and track). With one fixed-seed race per iteration, that draft could not be attributed to any cause, so I reject it.

What I kept, changed and rejected:
(1) Kept the iteration 0 controller exactly: base_speed 1.5, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, weights [1, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1], line_loss last_direction. Kept iteration 0 geometry exactly: sensors at y=0.06, x = +/-0.04, +/-0.02, 0; wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.8, body 0.12 x 0.16.
(2) Changed one factor only: sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016. Each sensor covers more of the 25 mm tape, so the sum of readings is less likely to fall below the 0.05 line-loss threshold on bends. Line loss occurred about once per run in all data, so this is the one change with a clear mechanism for reducing it.
(3) Rejected: the kp, kd, ki and base_speed changes from my draft, the wider or forward array, and the mass and track changes. Each is untested in isolation, and the critique showed none was tied to a measured signal value or speed.

Expected result: line_loss_events at or below iteration 0 (about 1.0 per run), and progress at or above 0.15. The score should be near or above 53. A result below 53 with the same progress would point to the larger footprint overlapping the centre signal.

Decision rule for the next revision: if line_loss_events falls and progress rises, keep sensor_size 0.016 and test kp next by itself. If line_loss_events is unchanged, sensor_size is not the limit, so revert it and test kp alone. If progress exceeds 0.9 with completion 0, raise base_speed by 0.1. If max_error exceeds 0.05 with low steering_oscillation, raise kp alone by 0.5.
